title: Code on Social Security, 2020: gig and platform workers
summary: This national law came into force on 21 November 2025. For the first time it recognises gig and platform workers and requires aggregators (platform companies) to contribute to a social security fund for them. Exact contribution rates and benefits are still being set through rules and schemes.
benefits: Legal recognition of gig and platform workers
Aggregators must pay into a social security fund. The law sets a range of 1% to 2% of annual turnover, capped at 5% of what they pay to gig workers
Benefits are delivered through notified schemes
how_to_apply: Register on e-Shram so you are on the list when benefits are notified
status_note: The law is in force but category-wise contribution rates and many scheme details were still being finalised as of mid-2026. Do not promise a specific benefit. Say what the law provides and that schemes are still being rolled out.

title: Rajasthan gig workers law (2023)
summary: Rajasthan was the first state to pass a law for platform-based gig workers, in 2023. It provides for registration of gig workers and a welfare board.
eligibility: Gig or platform worker working in Rajasthan
how_to_apply: Ask the Rajasthan labour department how to register and whether the board is operating
status_note: Passed in July 2023. Reports say implementation has been slow. Confirm on the state labour department's official channels.

title: Karnataka gig workers law (2025)
summary: Karnataka brought in a law for platform-based gig workers (an ordinance in May 2025 and a bill in August 2025). It sets up registration, a welfare fund and a welfare board.
eligibility: Gig or platform worker working in Karnataka
how_to_apply: Ask the Karnataka labour department how to register on the welfare board
status_note: A January 2026 report said the law was in effect but the welfare board was still awaiting notification. Check whether registration is open.

title: Bihar gig workers law (2025)
summary: Bihar passed a law in July 2025 for platform-based gig workers. It covers registration, a welfare fund and benefits such as insurance, accident cover, maternity support and old-age protection.
eligibility: Gig or platform worker working in Bihar
how_to_apply: Ask the Bihar labour department about registration
status_note: Passed in July 2025. Whether the fund and board are operating is not confirmed.

title: Jharkhand gig workers law (2025)
summary: Jharkhand passed a law in August 2025 covering registration, social security and a way to complain about the platform. Platforms can be penalised for breaking it, with fines reported up to Rs 10 lakh.
eligibility: Gig or platform worker working in Jharkhand
how_to_apply: Ask the Jharkhand labour department about registration and the complaint process
status_note: Passed in August 2025. Operational status of registration and grievance process is not confirmed.

title: Telangana gig workers law (2026)
summary: The Telangana assembly passed a platform-based gig workers bill in early 2026. It provides for a welfare board and a levy on platform transactions (reported at 1% to 2%) to fund insurance, pension and maternity benefits.
eligibility: Gig or platform worker working in Telangana
how_to_apply: Ask the Telangana labour department whether the law has been notified and registration is open
status_note: Passed by the assembly in early 2026. We could not confirm governor assent or notification, so do not tell a worker they can register yet.

title: Central guidelines for cab and bike-taxi aggregators (2025)
summary: The Ministry of Road Transport issued Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines in 2025 that set rules for cab and bike-taxi platforms, including how much of the fare drivers should get and insurance for drivers. States decide whether and how to adopt them.
benefits: Reported minimum driver share of the fare (about 80% for driver-owned vehicles) and health and term insurance for drivers. Confirm exact figures before quoting
status_note: These are central guidelines. They apply in a state only after the state adopts them. The numbers above were recalled from general knowledge and must be verified against the official guidelines.

title: Account blocked or deactivated by a platform
summary: If a platform blocks your ID, you can ask for the reason and appeal. Ask in writing, keep screenshots, use the platform's grievance officer, and escalate to the labour department or e-Shram helpline if there is no answer.
steps: Take screenshots of the block message, your ratings and your recent earnings
Ask the platform in writing, in the app or by email, for the exact reason and the right to appeal
Write to the platform's grievance officer. Platforms are expected to have one
If there is no reply, complain to your state labour department and call the e-Shram helpline 14434
Keep a record of dates, ticket numbers and names
status_note: Specific notice and appeal rights depend on the state law and the platform's own policy. Do not promise reinstatement. Offer a grievance draft instead.

title: Getting your wages on time and at least the minimum wage
summary: Workers are entitled to be paid at least the minimum wage for their state and job, and to be paid on time. For daily-wage work, payment is generally due at the end of the work period. Cutting pay or not paying is a labour complaint.
steps: Write down dates worked, the agreed rate and what was paid
Ask the contractor or employer for the due amount, preferably with a witness or by message
If unpaid, complain to the state labour department or Labour Commissioner office
Keep photos of attendance, messages and any payment proof
status_note: Minimum wage rates differ by state and job. Confirm the current notified rate with the state labour department.

title: Traffic challan: check, pay or contest
summary: You can check an e-challan and pay or contest it through the official Parivahan e-challan portal or the traffic court. Pay only through official channels and ask for a receipt. Keep your vehicle papers in DigiLocker or mParivahan.
steps: Check the challan on the official e-challan portal with your vehicle number
If it is wrong, contest it online or in the traffic court. Keep photos and papers
Pay only on the official portal or at an official counter and keep the receipt
Do not pay cash on the roadside without an official receipt

title: Free legal aid
summary: People who qualify can get a lawyer and legal advice for free through the legal services authorities. Eligibility depends on factors such as income and category. Ask at the District Legal Services Authority or call 15100.
how_to_apply: Call 15100 or visit the District Legal Services Authority office in your district court
